correctness.rationale: Parseval reduces squared Euler-row masses exactly to a Fourier average of (1-a)^j with 0≤a≤1; a geometric sum gives S_N. The integral exponential comparison evaluates exactly to N e^{-2Nβ}(I0+I1). Factoring e^{-Na}-(1-a)^N and e^{-a}-(1-a)≤a²/2 proves 0≤S_N-H_N<1/2 for every N and r. For β=λ/N and N≥8L, the expansion N log(1-x/N) with an explicit positive third-order tail bounds the remainder by (32L²/3+200L³/9)/N; angular integration yields K(λ). Endpoint and asymptotic regimes follow by continuity and standard fixed-order Bessel asymptotics. A 98-case finite checker replayed from the delivered source was corroborative only.

originality.rationale: The claim is a uniform finite-section Hilbert–Schmidt energy approximation and critical order-one correction. Direct comparisons with the 2014 Euler-space paper, the 2016 Tauberian preprint, 2017 binomial difference spaces, and 2020 binomial–Euler induced-operator norm show no statement or stronger implication covering these quantitative conclusions. The old binomial generating function is not counted as novel. value.rationale: The result measures the full squared singular-value mass of finite Euler summability operators rather than classical induced norms, and uniformly quantifies its smoothing-dependent transition with an absolute finite-size error and a nontrivial order-one Bessel correction on the natural β=λ/N scale. The exact parameter-reflection symmetry contrasts with induced-operator norms and gives a robust computational substitute for summing N(N+1)/2 binomial squares. The full dimension/parameter range is structurally motivated; not an arbitrary finite table or slight endpoint improvement.
